data.title: News of Further Layoffs Gives Intel Stock (NASDAQ:INTC) No Help
data.description:
Normally, layoffs do good things for stock prices, but chip stock Intel (INTC) found today that is not always the case. Intel employees revealed Intel's plans for new layoffs, and Intel stock slipped over 2% in Monday afternoon's trading, and Intel has seen a 60.7% rally in its share price over the past year.

Yes, Again

Back in September 2025, according to a report from Calcalis, Intel had a headcount of around 88,400. The newest headcount was down significantly, coming in at 81,100 as of September 2026. Now, Intel is set to fire more employees, this time focusing on the information technology (IT) division. Cuts started just two days ago, the report noted, but the extent and the overall geographical reach are somewhat unclear.

Intel released a statement which did not directly confirm layoffs, but certainly suggested they existed. The statement noted, "As part of our broader strategy to become a more focused and efficient company, we continually assess our workforce to ensure priorities and resources are appropriately aligned." Employee discussion platforms, meanwhile, provided further insight than Intel itself seemed willing to reveal, noting that the IT department suffered layoffs impacting "…a double-digit percentage of the department's workforce." This might get somewhat concerning going forward–especially if there are more layoffs beyond this–but Intel still has a small army of employees on hand which should help it keep the workflow going.

Team-Up with Microsoft

Meanwhile, Microsoft (MSFT) offered its own news about Intel, noting that the pair would step up a collaboration agreement that has already run for decades to step up Azure infrastructure. Under the expanded agreement, Intel would supply its Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge (EMIB) system to support cloud engineering at Microsoft.

The agreement also provides a supply of Xeon processors, including the upcoming Diamond Rapids line, to help drive Microsoft's cloud systems. Microsoft even plans to support Intel in the development and advancement of Compute Express Link (CXL), a tool designed to improve memory efficiency, along with Intel QuickAssist. The result should provide significant improvements, ranging from 2.3 times greater memory performance in cloud workloads to 2.5 times faster SQL backups. High-profile clients are vital to the overall health of Intel's foundry efforts, and Microsoft easily ranks among the highest-profile clients.

Is Intel a Buy, Hold or Sell?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Hold consensus rating on INTC stock based on seven Buys, 25 Holds and one Sell assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. The average INTC price target of $90.93 per share implies 66.49% upside potential.

data.title: AMD Stock Climbed 3% After OpenAI Said It Sped Up Chip Development
data.description:
Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) stock was up 3.3% on Wednesday after OpenAI said it helped the chipmaker speed up development of its processors. According to Greg Brockman, cofounder of the ChatGPT creator, the company's AI models were able to help AMD condense a year's worth of chip development down to just five months.

According to Brockman, the OpenAI models were able to achieve a 14% power, performance, and chip area improvement in AMD's flagship GPUs after five months. He claimed that this was equivalent to one year's worth of work for AMD's engineers. The OpenAI cofounder also said that improvements from this process have already started to be implemented into AMD's manufacturing.

AMD getting help from OpenAI makes sense. The two companies signed a collaboration agreement in October 2025 that brought AMD's chips to OpenAI's infrastructure. It's also known that AMD has been tweaking its chip designs to meet the needs of its customers. It also expanded its agreement with OpenAI in July 2026 to switch from just hardware to full-stack development.

What Else Has AMD Stock Up Today?

AMD stock was also up on Wednesday after rival chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA) released its Q3 2026 earnings report. Nvidia posted adjusted EPS and revenue that beat Wall Street's estimates. It also raised its guidance on the strong earnings results. This helped boost other semiconductor stocks today, even if NVDA stock didn't rise alongside them.

A strong earnings and guidance from Nvidia is a positive for AMD. It shows that ongoing demand in the chip sector remains strong amid the AI boom. That's important to AMD as it operates in the same markets and will also benefit from ongoing demand for AI CPUs and GPUs.

AMD's Recent Stock Movement

With AMD stock up over 3% today, the company has continued to rebound from a recent dip. Today's movement also built on its 135.06% year-to-date rally and a 118.6% gain over the past 12 months.

Even with today's rally, AMD stock didn't experience heavy trading. Only about 20 million shares have changed hands so far, compared to a three-month average daily trading volume of about 30.72 million shares.

Is AMD Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold?

Turning to Wall Street, the analysts' consensus rating for AMD is Strong Buy, based on 29 Buy and three Hold ratings over the past three months. With that comes an average AMD stock price target of $652.18, suggesting a possible 25.55% upside for the shares. (See AMD Stock Forecast)

data.title: Bill Ackman Blasts Nvidia Board Over Jensen Huang's Exit
data.description:
Billionaire investor Bill Ackman has accused chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA) of failing its shareholders by forcing out founder Jensen Huang without properly considering the consequences. The criticism comes after Nvidia's board rejected the possibility of Huang returning as CEO, even as the company reported record quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion, an increase of 103% year-over-year.

In a post on X, the CEO of investment firm Pershing Square (PS) argued that Nvidia's directors had rushed their decision following reports about Huang's personal relationships, which included allegations that involved a suspected Chinese spy.

Ackman questioned whether the board had enough time to examine the facts before accepting Huang's departure. He suggested that directors should have met in person and given themselves more time to consider a decision that could affect Nvidia's leadership for years.

He also argued that an inappropriate relationship with an employee does not automatically justify removing a CEO. According to Ackman, directors should examine the circumstances before deciding what action is appropriate.

His criticism comes after comments from Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones, who said on Tuesday that the board had unanimously accepted Huang's resignation and would not reinstate him. Huang had previously indicated that he would be willing to return if the board invited him.

Could Nvidia Shareholders Push for Huang's Return?

Ackman believes that shareholder pressure could force Nvidia's directors to reconsider. At a Semafor conference, he suggested that investors who want Huang back could request a special shareholder meeting.

Nvidia's rules allow shareholders to request such a meeting if they have collectively held at least 15% of the company's voting power for one year. Huang owned about 3.58% of Nvidia, according to its May proxy filing, meaning that he would need support from other qualifying shareholders.

Meanwhile, Nvidia's latest financial results show what is at stake. Adjusted earnings per share increased by 111% to $2.68, while data center revenue grew by 110% to $107.6 billion.

The company also forecast approximately $130 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, above Wall Street's expectations of roughly $125 billion.

For now, longtime finance chief Colette Kress remains the interim CEO while Nvidia searches for a permanent replacement. The board has also established an independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding Huang's departure.

What Is a Good Price for NVDA?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Moderate Buy consensus rating on Nvidia stock based on 30 Buys, 13 Holds, and one Sell assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. Furthermore, the average Nvidia price target of $232.59 per share implies 53.7% upside potential. (See NVDA Stock Forecast).

data.title: Fed Minutes Show More Rate Hikes Are Coming
data.description:
The latest meeting minutes from the U.S. Federal Reserve show consensus building for further interest rate hikes. The minutes from the central bank's last meeting on Oct. 27 and 28 show that members of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) are broadly in agreement that interest rates need to move higher to lower stubbornly high inflation.

"Almost all participants judged that, under their baseline outlooks for inflation and the labor market, further action to raise the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate, in order to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent objective," read the meeting minutes.

At the October meeting, Fed officials also expressed growing concerns about artificial intelligence (AI) and its potential impact on inflation. The meeting minutes show that policymakers spent considerable time discussing AI, and that they view the technology as "a material source of inflation risk."

Inflation in America

Data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics showed that inflation in the U.S. was at an annualized rate of 4% in October of this year, double the Federal Reserve's stated 2% target. The American central bank, led by Chair Kevin Warsh, raised interest rates by 25 basis points in September, the first time it has tightened monetary policy in three years. At the October meeting, the Fed voted to hold its benchmark interest rate in its current range of 3.75% to 4%.

Financial markets are pricing in a 98% chance that the Fed raises interest rates another 25 basis points at the conclusion of its next policy meeting on Dec. 9, according to data from LSEG (LSEG). The latest meeting minutes from the central bank reinforce this case with a majority of Fed Governors agreeing that more action is needed to lower consumer prices.

Fed Governor Waller's Comments

Earlier on Nov. 18, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said during an interview on CNBC that the Federal Reserve might need to "shock people" with a 50 basis point interest rate hike in December as inflation continues to rise more than expected throughout the U.S.

"I'm very, very concerned about inflation. It's kind of headed in the wrong direction, and it's spreading out," said Waller when speaking to CNBC. "If you really want to get it down, you've got to start taking more aggressive actions."

Despite Waller's calls for more aggressive action from the U.S. central bank, financial markets see little chance that the Federal Reserve will raise rates by 50 basis points in December. LSEG tracking shows that traders are pricing in only a 5% chance that the central bank will increase interest rates by half a percentage point at its final meeting of the year.

The U.S. Inflation Rate

Below is a chart from TipRanks that looks at the annualized inflation rate in the U.S. over the past year. As one can see, inflation has remained consistently above the Federal Reserve's 2% target.

data.title: Boeing Stock (NYSE:BA) Slips With New B-1 Weapons Pylon
data.description:
Aerospace stock Boeing (BA) has a lot invested in defense operations. So when word from Defence Industry Europe discussed the new B-1 weapons pylon, it was the kind of point that should have raised eyebrows. Boeing stock slipped fractionally in Wednesday afternoon's trading. Boeing has also seen a 13.56% loss in its share price over the past year.

Tomorrow's Weapons, Today's Hardpoint

Boeing's new external weapons pylon for the B-1 bomber recently passed what is known as critical design review. This allows Boeing to put together the necessary hardware and software to actually build the thing and test it accordingly. Once this is built it may have a significant impact on how the B-1 bomber works as the new pylon could ultimately double the B-1 bomber's payload capacity.

Perhaps more importantly the new pylon would also give it the capability of bringing in new kinds of weapons, including hypersonic munitions. It is known as the Load Adaptable Modular (LAM) pylon, which uses six standard hardpoints that were originally intended to handle Air-Launched Cruise Missiles. With this new pylon in place, B-1 bombers would become more adaptable to mission conditions and could be used with more types of missions.

New Cabins

Meanwhile, a report from Simple Flying showed off planned new cabins on the 777-9 for Singapore Airlines. The new cabins will not be available until 2027, but when they are, they should deliver a new level of passenger comfort that might even justify airline ticket prices these days. Simple Flying saw the cabins at an exhibition center in Singapore, and the results were impressive.

One of the biggest changes came to Singapore Airlines' business class flights. It featured more leg room, and had a feeling more "spacious" overall, to one passenger who had flown Singapore Airlines business class previously. Singapore Airlines also built what it describes as "the largest double bed in the sky," which should be welcome for those long-haul travelers. In fact, Simple Flying reports described it as the kind of thing that needed to be experienced rather than merely seen; no one chooses a seat for color schemes, after all, but rather for space, size and comfort, a point that needed more than pictures to convey.

Is Boeing a Good Stock to Buy Right Now?

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on BA stock based on 18 Buys and one Hold assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. The average BA price target of $235.35 per share implies 43.6% upside potential.

data.title: U.S. Stock Indices Are Volatile as Nvidia's Earnings Rally Fades
data.description:
U.S. stocks were volatile on Wednesday despite strong earnings from chipmaker Nvidia (NVDA). At the time of writing, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (DIA) fell by 0.6%, while the S&P 500 (SPY) gained by 0.2%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq 100 (QQQ) rose by 0.8%. Nvidia shares also reversed an initial 2.7% gain and were down by 1.6%.

The reversal came despite Nvidia reporting fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8 billion, an increase of 103% year-over-year. Adjusted earnings per share rose by 111% to $2.68, beating estimates of $2.48. The company also forecast fourth-quarter revenue of approximately $130 billion, above Wall Street's expectations of roughly $125 billion.

However, the results were not enough to offset concerns about Nvidia's future following Jensen Huang's departure as CEO.

Meanwhile, Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller added to uncertainty after telling CNBC that a half-percentage-point interest rate increase may be necessary in December to control inflation. The Fed held rates at 3.75% to 4% in October, and minutes from that meeting are scheduled to be released at 2 p.m. ET today.

Oil prices also declined after government data showed that U.S. crude inventories increased by 3.4 million barrels last week, compared with expectations for an increase of just 58,000 barrels. Brent crude fell 2.2% to $92.41 per barrel, while WTI crude was down 3.1% to $83.11.

Retail Earnings and Anthropic IPO Add to Market Activity

Outside technology stocks, big-box retailer Target (TGT) jumped by 5.6% following stronger-than-expected quarterly results. Revenue grew by 7.1% to $27.1 billion, while adjusted earnings reached $2.65 per share. However, that figure included a $0.50 benefit from tariff refunds.

Home improvement retailer Lowe's (LOW) moved in the opposite direction, declining by 0.3% despite reporting revenue growth of 9.3% to $22.8 billion. Adjusted earnings reached $3.10 per share, including a $0.34 benefit from tariff refunds. Lowe's also increased its full-year sales forecast to $92.5 billion from $92 billion.

Separately, AI developer Anthropic (ANT) is expected to price its initial public offering today ahead of its anticipated Nasdaq (NDAQ) debut on Thursday, November 19, under the ticker ANT.

data.title: Healthcare Stocks: UnitedHealth (UNH), Humana (HUM), Cigna (CI) and Others Fall on Proposed CRUSH Rule
data.description:
Healthcare stocks took a beating on Wednesday after the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) proposed a new rule that would result in stricter regulation of the sector. Specifically, this could affect companies that operate through Medicare, Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program (CHIP), and the Health Insurance Marketplace.

This new rule is called the Comprehensive Regulations to Uncover Suspicious Healthcare (CRUSH). Its purpose is to identify instances of overcharges from insurance providers via increased audits. This could also require insurance companies to repay those overcharges. CMS said that this new rule could save taxpayers $90 billion over the next decade.

While the CRUSH rule has investors in insurance companies worried today, it could be some time before it is implemented. Comments on the rule will be allowed until Jan. 19, 2027, and it could face legal pushback. Oppenheimer analysts argued the rule could face the same fate as similar proposals that were made in 2025 and squashed in a federal court.

How Healthcare Stocks Reacted to the CRUSH Rule Proposal

Health insurance companies didn't fare well on Wednesday in light of the new CRUSH rule.

  • UnitedHealth (UNH) stock was down 8.85% today.
  • Humana (HUM) stock fell 10.65% as of this writing.
  • Cigna (CI) stock retreated 2.75% on Wednesday.
  • CVS (CVS) stock dipped 3.48%.
  • Elevance Health (ELV) stock decreased 6.13% this afternoon.
  • Centene (CNC) stock dropped 5.6% on the news.
  • Molina Healthcare (MOH) stock took a 5.42% beating today.
  • Oscar Health (OSCR) stock pulled back 5.43% as of this writing.

Which Healthcare Stocks Are Worth Buying on Today's Fall?

Turning to the TipRanks stock comparison tool, traders can see which of these healthcare stocks are worth investing in. UnitedHealth, Humana, and CVS stand out from the pack with their Strong Buy consensus ratings. Among those three, CVS offers the highest upside potential at 28.35% with its $110.13 price target, followed by UnitedHealth with an upside potential of 23.87% with its $482.69 price target, and Humana with its upside potential of 14.74% with a $508.68 price target.

Healthcare stocks that investors may want to avoid include Molina Healthcare and Oscar Health, both of which have consensus Hold ratings. MOH stock also has a downside potential of 3.71% based on its $213 price target, while OSCR stock has an upside potential of 20.22% based on its $35.88 price target. data.title: Bending Spoons (BSP) Faces Another Earnings Test After Its $1.68B IPO
data.description:
Italian software group Bending Spoons (BSP) is preparing to release its third-quarter earnings on Friday, November 20, before the market opens. The results will mark the company's second earnings release following its $1.68 billion initial public offering (IPO) on Nasdaq in July. It also marks another major test for the company. Its full-year sales forecast, issued during the second-quarter earnings call in August, disappointed investors.

What Wall Street Expects from Bending Spoons' Q3 Results

For the third quarter, Wall Street expects revenue to rise 6% from the previous quarter to $745.86 million. Earnings per share are expected to be $0.32.

During the second quarter, the company surpassed analysts' expectations. It reported revenue of $704 million, beating the Wall Street consensus of $685 million. This marked a 126% growth from the same period last year.

Its adjusted earnings per share also topped expectations. The figure came in at $0.46, far above analysts' consensus estimate of $0.27. However, the full-year sales forecast of $2.78 billion to $2.82 billion fell short of consensus.

What Investors Will Watch

Investors will watch whether Bending Spoons maintains or raises its full-year sales estimates. They will also watch organic growth.

In the previous quarter, the company reported only 3% growth in its existing business. The headline growth rate of 126% was driven by its new software acquisitions.

The acquired companies include the internet brand AOL and the online ticketing platform Eventbrite. It also recently acquired the time-tracking tool Harvest and the mileage-tracking app MileIQ.

Investors will also watch for comments on the rise of AI tools. Bending Spoons' earnings need to show that AI tools do not pose an immediate threat to the company's software portfolio. Interestingly, Bank of America's (BAC) five-star analyst Omar Dessouky has argued that AI disruption to the company's business is uncertain and likely to be gradual.

Is Bending Spoons a Good Stock to Buy?

On Wall Street, analysts rate Bending Spoons shares a Moderate Buy. This reflects three Buys, one Hold, and one Sell rating issued over the past three months.

However, the average BSP price target of $45.20 implies about 5% upside (see BSP stock forecast here).

data.title: Cybersecurity Stocks Surge as U.S. Warns of AI-Powered Attacks
data.description:
Cybersecurity stocks climbed on Wednesday morning after Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin warned Congress about foreign hackers and the use of advanced AI in cyberattacks. Cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks (PANW) rose by roughly 6%, while cloud-security provider Netskope (NTSK) jumped by 10%. The rally comes as Palo Alto prepares to report its fiscal first-quarter earnings after the closing bell.

During testimony before the House Homeland Security Committee, Mullin said that Iranian government-linked hackers had targeted U.S. infrastructure since the conflict with Iran began earlier this year. He explained that attacks since February have increasingly targeted transportation and healthcare networks. Water and energy systems have also been targeted.

In addition, Mullin warned about North Korean hackers who use phishing attacks to steal information from government institutions. In addition, he said that criminals are using advanced AI technology to carry out more attacks and identify potential targets.

Palo Alto Networks Earnings Could Provide More Insight

The rally comes at an important time for Palo Alto Networks. Wall Street expects the company to report adjusted earnings of $0.97 per share on revenue of $3.31 billion. That would represent revenue growth of about 34% from the $2.47 billion reported a year earlier.

However, revenue growth is only part of what analysts will examine. Palo Alto expects annual recurring revenue from its next-generation security business to reach between $9.54 billion and $9.56 billion, an increase of 63% year-over-year.

This figure measures the annual value of recurring revenue from newer security products, which helps show how much demand is translating into ongoing customer contracts.

Last quarter, Palo Alto reported revenue of $3.41 billion, an increase of 34% year-over-year. The company also generated $1.3 billion in adjusted free cash flow. For Fiscal 2027, management has forecast revenue of between $14.1 billion and $14.2 billion, which equates to growth of 23% to 24%.

Is PANW Stock a Good Buy?

Turning to Wall Street, TipRanks data shows that analysts have a Strong Buy consensus rating on PANW stock. This is based on 32 Buys and eight Holds assigned in the past three months. Furthermore, the average PANW price target of $411.76 per share implies 25.8% upside potential. (See PANW Stock Forecast).
